trust_decision.summary: SyncHTTPHandler._check_auth decides whether a request may touch the sync event log; when --jwt-secret is configured it base64-decodes only the payload (and an optional exp) and never verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature, so any 'Bearer <header>.<payload>.<anything>' is accepted for /sync/pull, /sync/push and /sync/status.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary points at JWT verification in the sync server; the comment '# Minimal JWT decode without dependencies' at line 106 marks the decoder inside the guard every sync endpoint calls, so an engineer opens _check_auth first.

fix_sites.module_kind: stdlib HTTP request handler, auth guard branch
helper methods added to the same handler class

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: API-key bearer mode must keep working: when --api-key is set the same Authorization header carries an opaque shared key, and the unset-auth default must stay open for local runs; an over-broad rewrite that sends every Bearer token through the JWT verifier breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: compact HS256 JWT with exactly three dot-separated parts (fix.diff:50-52)
header alg other than HS256, e.g. {"alg":"none"} (fix.diff:56-58)
non-ASCII signature that makes hmac.compare_digest raise TypeError (fix.diff:66-68)
segment that decodes to a non-dict JSON value (fix.diff:41-43)
exp present as number (past/future) and exp present as non-numeric string (fix.diff:72-80)
no exp claim at all, still accepted (fix.diff:72-73)
jwt_secret not configured while the JWT branch is reached (fix.diff:47-48)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second Bearer guard on the MCP SSE transport that also accepts compact JWTs, copying the minimal payload-only decode instead of the hmac.compare_digest it uses today.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo already ships a second HTTP surface with its own hand-written bearer middleware and documents both transports; extending it to --jwt-secret is a natural copy of the sync server's check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The Hermes sync adapter validates a token it received with the same minimal decode (duplicated at hermes_memory_provider/sync_adapter.py:378).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The adapter is shipped as two identical copies and already builds the 'Authorization: Bearer' header itself, so a maintainer adding the documented MNEMOSYNE_SYNC_JWT support there would re-implement the check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third stdlib BaseHTTPRequestHandler in-tree that today has no auth; the same JWT gate could be added around it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It uses the identical stdlib handler idiom as the sync server (HTTPServer + BaseHTTPRequestHandler), so a sibling verifier written by the same author is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A JWT gate on the FastAPI memory browser before /api/search and /detail.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the only FastAPI surface in the project and is meant to be exposed remotely, so protecting it with the same --jwt-secret would look reasonable to a maintainer.

O9_family: CWE-347 improper verification of cryptographic signature (JWT auth bypass); family: authentication / signature-verification

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools/pip, pytest; core is zero-dependency, optional extras sync (cryptography) and embeddings
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_sync.py (~17 tests: event log, encryption roundtrip, then e2e plaintext/encrypted client-server sync using api_key at tests/test_sync.py:223-266); no JWT tests exist at the pinned commit; tests/test_s1_mcp_sse_auth.py covers the separate MCP bearer middleware.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep the existing minimal decoder and bolt on a signature compare in _check_auth (often with == on the base64 text or by only rejecting alg 'none'), then validate with the forged-token case the report gives and stop.
